chunk_findings.detail: `fail_closed_data` only traverses `Mapping`, `list`, and `tuple`; any other container is returned unchanged. For example, a failed redaction of a value containing a provider secret in a `set`/`frozenset` (`fail_closed_data({"sk-123"})`) returns `{"sk-123"}` with the secret intact. If that set is later rendered into a committed event shard, the raw secret reaches the log, violating the fail-closed requirement. It should traverse sets/frozensets or reject unsupported container types instead of falling through to `return value`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/redact_errors.py:40

chunk_findings.detail: The `openai` pattern `sk-(?:proj-|svcacct-|admin-)?[0-9A-Za-z_-]{20,}` matches any token beginning with `sk-` followed by 20 characters from a permissive alphabet. A legitimate event line containing `[REDACTED]` causes `shape_hit` to return `"openai"`, so `check_event_secrets` will treat a non-secret job/package/file identifier as an OpenAI key and refuse or redact the commit.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/secret_shapes.py SHAPES openai

chunk_findings.detail: The advertised generic `key = value` shape does not match plain `key` assignments: the prefix alternation is `(?:api[-_]?key|secret|token|passw(?:or)?d)`. Given `key = 1234567890Abcdefghij`, no provider pattern matches and `assigned-secret` misses it, so a long arbitrary secret assigned to the common variable name `key` is not redacted from the committed event log.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/secret_shapes.py SHAPES assigned-secret

chunk_findings.detail: Provider shape character classes do not allow newlines, so a provider key split across a line wrap bypasses detection. For example `AIzaABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ\n1234567890` is not matched by `shape_hit` on the full text, and a line-by-line check sees two fragments each below the minimum run; the raw pieces still reach the committed event log, violating the fail-closed goal for secrets split across lines.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/secret_shapes.py shape_hit

chunk_findings.detail: An added shard line whose content begins with `++ ` is misparsed as a `+++` file header. `git diff` emits that file line as `+++ [REDACTED]` (one leading `+` diff marker plus the two leading `+` and space from the content). The branch `raw.startswith("+++ ")` fires, sets `path = raw[4:]`, and never calls `line_hit` on the line. So a staged event shard line `++ [REDACTED]` is completely skipped and the secret is not scanned, allowing the commit to pass.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/enforce_secrets.py:64

chunk_findings.detail: `git diff --cached` is run without `--no-textconv`. `--no-ext-diff` does not disable textconv; if a `.gitattributes` file gives the event shard path a `diff=<driver>` with a configured `diff.<driver>.textconv`, the diff output `added_hits` sees is the converted output, not the staged raw blob. A textconv command that replaces key-shaped text with `REDACTED` makes `added_hits` see no shape hit while the staged shard retains the raw credential and is committed.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/enforce_secrets.py:89

chunk_findings.detail: `--diff-filter=ACMR` excludes the typechange status `T`. A staged change from a symlink `.ddflow/events/1` to a regular file containing `[REDACTED]` is not emitted at all by this command, so `added_hits` is empty and `check_event_secrets` returns `OK`; the secret-containing regular file is committed without being scanned.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/enforce_secrets.py:97

chunk_findings.detail: The new fail-closed branch returns `fail_closed_text()`, while the normal branch returns the two-tuple `red.text, red.total`. A non-`PatternError` exception from `redactor("log", cfg).text(text)`—the exact case this branch is meant to handle—therefore makes `_redact_event_text` return a placeholder string instead of a `(text, total)` tuple. Existing callers that unpack the two-tuple (`redacted_text, redacted_count = _redact_event_text(...)`) will raise `ValueError: too many values to unpack`, so the fail-closed path crashes event logging rather than writing a safe placeholder.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/sessions.py:66

chunk_findings.detail: The test asserts `S.redact(blob, cfg)[1] == 0` for `blob = "Zm9v" + KEYS["google"] + "bar"`. That string still contains a complete Google API key shape (`AIza` + 35 filler characters) but it is surrounded by adjacent word characters, so the boundary-sensitive shape match is skipped. This is a concrete bypass: an event line such as `{"text":"Zm9vAIzaFAKEFAKEFAKEFAKEFAKEbar"}` will be written unchanged to a shard, and `check_event_secrets`, which uses the same `shape_hit`, will not block it even though the provider key shape is present in the committed log line, violating the intent that provider key shapes never reach the committed event log.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_redact_provider_keys.py:test_a_shape_inside_a_longer_word_is_left_alone

Given event text `mysk-proj-abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz123`, `shape_hit` starts at `sk-proj-...` but the negative lookbehind sees the preceding `y` and rejects the match, so the raw `sk-proj-...` key is neither redacted nor blocked from the committed shard.

chunk_findings.detail: The fail-closed replacement only replaces mapping values; mapping keys are returned unchanged in `return {k: fail_closed_data(v) for k, v in value.items()}`. A provider key appearing as a JSON object key survives, for example `fail_closed_data({"AIza" + "A"*35: "x"})` yields `{"[REDACTED]": "[REDACTED]"}`. When that result is serialized into a committed event shard, the raw `AIza...` key is written to the log, so this fail-closed path still leaks a provider secret despite the “all text” requirement.

chunk_findings.detail: The newly added test `test_merging_in_a_line_the_other_parent_already_committed_is_not_refused` encodes a fail-open path. The merge commit therefore adds a provider key line to this branch’s committed event log, but `check_event_secrets` is asserted to return 0. A side branch containing a secret, committed before the guard existed or with hooks bypassed, can be merged into the protected branch without refusal, so the raw secret reaches the committed event log. chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/enforce_secrets.py check_event_secrets

chunk_findings.detail: The revised `openai` pattern still false-positives on harmless `sk-` identifiers that contain a digit. Given a staged event line `{"text": "[REDACTED]"}`, `shape_hit` sees a token starting with `sk-`, at least 20 trailing `[0-9A-Za-z_-]` characters, and the digit `2`, so it returns `"openai"`; `check_event_secrets` will refuse or redact this non-secret identifier. The added test only checks a digitless hyphenated name (`[REDACTED]`), so it does not catch this remaining false positive.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/secret_shapes.py SHAPES openai

chunk_findings.detail: Previous finding 3 still holds for the bare key case. `shape_hit("key = 1234567890Abcdefghij")` still produces no `assigned-secret` hit because the alternation omits the plain name `key`. data.command: [REDACTED:path] -m ddflow review fix-Bsecbug-redact-google-api-key --gate critic --intent 'Security fix: redact provider API key shapes (core/secret_shapes.py) from all text written to the committed event log, fail closed on redaction errors (core/redact_errors.py), refuse a commit that adds an event shard line matching a provider key shape (services/enforce_secrets.py, wired in enforce.check_commit). Rubber_duck found and we fixed 14 issues. ATTACK IT: pattern bypasses, ReDoS, fail-open paths where raw text reaches a shard, false positives blocking legitimate commits, commit-check blind spots.'

chunk_findings.detail: For `Mapping` values, keys are sanitized only when the key itself is a direct `str` that does not match `_PLAIN_KEY`; any non-`str` key is returned unchanged by `_key` and is never passed through `fail_closed_data`. This violates the function’s “every string leaf replaced” contract and creates a fail-open path for raw text. Concrete input: `fail_closed_data({("Authorization", "sk-1234567890"): "x"})` returns `{("Authorization", "sk-1234567890"): "[REDACTED:redaction-failed]"}`. If that value is written to a committed event shard after a redaction failure, the raw provider-key-shaped string in the tuple key reaches the log. `frozenset` and `bytes` keys containing text are also left untouched.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/redact_errors.py:fail_closed_data

chunk_findings.detail: `shape_hit("userAKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE")` returns `""` even though the text contains the AWS access key ID `[REDACTED]`, because the fixed-width left guard `(?<![0-9A-Za-z])` rejects the prefix when it is pasted after an alphanumeric token such as `user`. A shard line like `userAKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE` is a raw provider credential but is missed by both redaction and commit enforcement, so the raw key reaches the event log.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/secret_shapes.py:28

chunk_findings.detail: The `openai-project` and `stripe` patterns have no left boundary guard, so ordinary identifiers match provider shapes. `shape_hit("ta[REDACTED]")` returns `"openai-project"` because the substring `sk-proj-` starts at the `s` in "task", and `shape_hit("ta[REDACTED]")` returns `"stripe"` because the substring `sk_live_` starts at the `s` in "task". Since these same shapes drive commit enforcement, a legitimate event-shard line such as `task_live_...` or `task-proj-...` is refused.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/secret_shapes.py:22 and :31

chunk_findings.detail: When `[enforce].event_secrets = "block"` and `_new_hits` returns `None` because Git cannot produce the staged diff, this branch returns `Verdict(OK, ...)`. A concrete triggering input is an unborn branch/initial commit: `git diff --cached HEAD -- .ddflow/events` fails with `fatal: ambiguous argument 'HEAD'`, so `_diff` returns `None` and the check passes even though a staged hand-edited event shard may contain an unredacted provider key. That is a fail-open path for the stated security backstop: the commit is not refused, and the raw key can reach the committed event log. The comment's justification (“a repository with no readable index has nothing staged to leak”) is not true for an unborn HEAD with a readable index.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/enforce_secrets.py:139 (`check_event_secrets`)

chunk_findings.detail: On a non-`PatternError` exception from `redactor("log", cfg).text(text)`, the new code returns `fail_closed_text()` directly. The success path returns `(red.text, red.total)`, so callers expect a 2-tuple. If `fail_closed_text()` returns the placeholder string (as its name and the `core/redact_errors.py` helper indicate), a redaction failure makes `redact_log_text` return a string, and a caller doing `redacted, total = redact_log_text(...)` raises `ValueError` (or unpacks individual characters if the placeholder is exactly two chars). The fallback should return `(fail_closed_text(), 0)` or otherwise match the success-path tuple shape.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/sessions.py:66 (redact_log_text)

chunk_findings.detail: The test explicitly asserts that a merge commit introducing an event shard line containing a provider key shape is not refused. In the scenario, `other` already committed a shard line with `KEYS["google"]`; after diverging, `git merge --no-commit other` stages that raw key into the default branch’s index, yet `ES.check_event_secrets(repo, Config()).exit == 0`. A following `git commit` would complete the merge and add the raw key to `.ddflow/events/a.jsonl` on the merged branch, even though that merge commit adds an event shard line matching a provider key shape relative to its first parent. This is a fail-open commit-check blind spot and violates the stated fix requirement to refuse a commit that adds such a shard line.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_redact_provider_keys.py:test_merging_in_a_line_the_other_parent_already_committed_is_not_refused

chunk_findings.detail: `_PLAIN_KEY` keeps any all-lowercase/digit/underscore string of at most 32 characters as a mapping key. A Stripe live/test secret has the form `sk_live_<24 alphanumeric>` / `sk_test_<24 alphanumeric>` (one of the built-in provider shapes), and `[REDACTED]` is exactly 32 characters, all lower/digits/underscore, so `_key` returns it unchanged. Consequently `fail_closed_data({"[REDACTED]": "x"})` yields that raw Stripe key in the output, replacing only the value. If that sanitized mapping is serialized into a committed event shard, the raw credential is still logged, violating the fail-closed guarantee for redaction failures.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/redact_errors.py:34 (_PLAIN_KEY / _key)

chunk_findings.detail: The previous `_L` bypass was only fixed for the `sk-proj-`/`sk-svcacct-`/`sk-admin-` project prefixes. The legacy OpenAI shape still uses `_L + r"sk-(?=...)[0-9A-Za-z]{20,}"`, so a raw legacy key glued to preceding alphanumeric text is not matched. Concrete input: `shape_hit("xsk-Abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz123")` returns `""`; the same string with a delimiter before `sk-` would match `"openai"`. `check_event_secrets` will therefore neither redact nor reject the leaked provider key, preserving the fail-open bypass.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/secret_shapes.py:29

chunk_findings.detail: The revised legacy `openai` pattern still flags a plain all-alphanumeric non-secret identifier: `shape_hit("[REDACTED]")` returns `"openai"`. A staged event line containing such a correlation/job ID will be refused or redacted even though it is not an OpenAI credential. The added false-positive test only covers a digitless/hyphenated name; it does not cover this all-alphanumeric numeric ID.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/secret_shapes.py:29

chunk_findings.detail: The test blesses a fail-open merge path: `git merge --no-commit other` stages a provider-key-shaped shard line into the current branch's `.ddflow/events/a.jsonl`, and the test asserts `ES.check_event_secrets(repo, Config()).exit == 0`. The ensuing merge commit's diff against its first parent introduces that `google` key line into this branch's committed event log, so a pre-commit hook using this check would allow the merge and the key would reach the branch's event shard. The earlier refutation that the line "already committed in the other parent is already in history" does not answer this: refusing the merge before commit would keep this branch's event log clean. This is exactly a commit adding a shard line with a key shape that the change's intent says to refuse.
